chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan and ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad narrated to me, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Muʿāwiyah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who stood in the obligatory salat (prayer), then became forgetful and thought that it was a supererogatory prayer, or who stood in the supererogatory prayer and thought that it was obligatory. He said: “It is according to what he began the salat (prayer) upon.”

key_terms.فَسَهَا: he became forgetful or inattentive during prayer

ai.seo_question: If someone mistakenly thinks an obligatory salat (prayer) is a nafilah, or vice versa, how is the prayer judged?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning confusion during salat (prayer) between an obligatory and a supererogatory prayer. The Imam عليه السلام states that the prayer is judged according to the intention and basis upon which it was originally begun.
